title: Route-specific KV-cache-aware SLI spec and eviction protocol
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Purpose: define a route-aware SLI specification that accounts for KV cache behavior and a deterministic eviction/crediting protocol to drive fair load-shedding and multi-region failover decisions. Motivation: during the FEB 2026 incident (INC-2026-02) tail latency and burn-rate were concentrated on conversational routes with high prefix reuse but frequent cache churn. Current SLI definitions (global p99 / availability) mask per-route cache sensitivity and lead to noisy eviction decisions that penalize cold routes or routes that benefit from prefix reuse.

Goals: 
1) Define per-route SLI buckets (interactive vs batch vs streaming) with explicit numerator/denominator and windowing.
2) Attribute SLI measurements to an "effective token" model that discounts tokens satisfied by KV cache hits to avoid double-penalizing served work.
3) Establish an eviction-credit system that: a) preserves latency SLOs for high-priority routes, b) allows borrowing/lending of error-budget credits across variants and regions, and c) integrates with circuit breakers for graceful degradation.

SLI definitions (proposed): 
- Availability (route R, window W=5m): numerator = number of successful responses from primary variant meeting latency and correctness predicates; denominator = total requests for route R received at the ingress. Success predicate: end-to-end latency <= L_R threshold AND model response scored OK by automated quality checks (where applicable).
- Tail latency p99 (route R, window W=1h): measured on observed end-to-end latency after prefix/KV substitution.
- Effective compute tokens per request (ECT): raw_generated_tokens - kv_cache_hit_tokens. Use ECT to normalize cost and to assign burn rate to error budget.

KV-cache-aware measurement rules: 
- Track per-request kv_cache_hits (token count) and raw_generated_tokens in tracing ctx; report ECT to metrics.
- SLIs that are cost-normalized (e.g., error budget burn rate) will use ECT-weighted denominators so routes benefiting from cache reuse do not appear artificially cheap.
- For latency SLIs, measurements use observed latency but annotate whether latency is from cache-hit (low compute) vs cache-miss (high compute). This allows separate SLI curves for cache-hit vs cache-miss cohorts.

Eviction and crediting protocol (high level): 
- Each route R has an SLI band and an assigned priority tier (P0,P1,P2).
- Eviction credits = accumulated budget from consistent under-utilization (defined as sustained ECT per-minute below planned baseline). Credits are earned at a rate defined in the routing config and are capped.
- When capacity pressure occurs, eviction algorithm traverses candidate list by: 1) routes with negative burn-rate delta (over-spenders), 2) lowest priority tier, 3) lowest eviction credits, 4) highest ECT per request.
- Preemption steps: soft-throttle (rate-limit), quality downgrade (quantized model variant), pin-to-cache-cohort (prefer cached variant), then full eviction (circuit-breaker/truncate). Each step has a configured escalation delay and a short-form SLO gate that can halt escalation if OK.
- Canary & pinned variants: pinned routes (customer-requested model pin) are eligible for eviction credits transfer only if explicitly allowed by contract; otherwise they are preempted only after softer measures.

Error budget transfers & multi-region interactions: 
- Error-budget transfer can be initiated by a regional aribter when a route's primary region is capacity constrained. Transfers deduct credits from donors and add to recipients with an audit log entry (trace id + manual approval for transfers larger than X%).
- When failover to a secondary region occurs, SLIs are measured per-region and aggregated with weights. Burndown attribution: primary-region burn continues to be charged to primary until a full cutover window completes. Short-term borrow is recorded as an escrowed debt that must be reconciled within 24h.

Circuit-breaker thresholds (suggested): 
- Soft-open: sustained p95 latency > 1.5x target for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows. Action: enable soft-throttle and start losing eviction credits at double rate.
- Open: sustained p99 > 2x target AND error budget burn > 2x expected for 15 minutes. Action: force downgrade to compatible variant and reroute 30% of new traffic to fallback.
- Closed: automatic when p99 <= target for 30 minutes AND normalized burn < 0.8x for 1h.

Observability & dashboards: 
- New grafana panels per-route: ECT histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, p50/p95/p99 split by cache-hit vs cache-miss, eviction_credits ledger, and transfer audit log.
- Tracing: add two tags to span: kv_cache_hits and effective_tokens. Add decision trace when eviction is applied (eviction_reason, credits_before, credits_after).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Implementation instruments ECT and kv_cache_hits at ingress + runtime; metrics emitted for each route.
- Eviction protocol implemented in simulator and validated in perf-lab at 10k rps sustained with mixed cache hit rates.
- Console UIs surface eviction credits and a historical timeline of evictions/transfers for each route.
- Run a canary for runtime-1.22 in us-west-2, validate error-budget transfer behavior with a synthetic donor route.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Attribution complexity: ECT relies on accurate token counting; model-level instrumentation required and may add small overhead.
- Behavioral complexity: eviction-credit markets introduce non-obvious outcomes for tenants; require clear Console explanations and conservative defaults.

Next steps / Implementation plan: 
1) Instrumentation spike (ENG-512345) – 3d: add kv token counters and emit ECT.
2) Simulator & policy code (ENG-517890) – 5d: implement eviction algorithm and run synthetic scenarios.
3) Dashboard & Console affordance (DES-2190 + PM review) – 4d.
4) Canary & rollout (runtime-1.22) – 7d.
